# Vault invitations and requester authorization

The vault has one **Invite to vault** button. The owner chooses a current Slack
member, checks which saved logins, API keys and payment cards to share, then
confirms use of only that selection on their behalf. Nothing is checked for a
new member, and credentials added later stay private. **People with access**
groups each member's shared credentials; **Edit access** reopens the checklist
with that member's existing selection, and **Remove** revokes their access.
The member sees **Shared with you** in their vault. An
invitation takes effect immediately. When the selection adds credentials,
Clanker sends one private Slack DM to the recipient with the sharer's Slack
mention, the number of newly shared credentials, and an **Open vault** button.
The message includes no credential titles, identifiers, grant handles, secrets,
or authenticated link tokens. Unchanged saves and removal-only edits send no DM.
The vault confirms Slack delivery or reports that delivery could not be
confirmed; access remains saved in either case. Delivery is bounded to ten
seconds and is not retried automatically. Slack's own notification settings
control whether the DM also produces a push notification.
The saved credential remains in the owner's encrypted native vault. The guest
receives a grant handle and metadata, not a copied vault entry.

This implements explicit delegation. It does **not** establish that the reported
Gmail disclosure is fixed in the running system. The gateway has not been
reloaded, no real invitation has been created, and the consumer browser
provider's isolation and cookie-deletion behavior remain unverified.

## Permission boundary

Slack OIDC establishes the owner of the vault web session. Owner and workspace
come from that session, never request-body fields. CSRF and exact-origin checks
cover invite and revoke. Only native items in that owner's vault can be invited;
guests cannot pass an invited handle to create another invitation.

A durable grant binds workspace, owner, recipient and selected credential.
Saving a member's checklist validates the entire selection and applies all
permission additions/removals in one database transaction. Invalid or foreign
items cause no partial changes. Still-selected credentials retain their grant
handles; unchecked credentials and their pending approvals are revoked before
browser cleanup. Selecting credentials grants no wildcard access to the vault.
Its identity binding includes kind, origin, account identifier and creation
time. The runtime resolves that grant for the authenticated requesting member,
checks current membership of both parties, and verifies the selected native item
still exists with that binding. An unrelated native handle, another member's
grant, a removed or changed account, or a disabled member is denied. Reinvitation
after revocation produces a new grant handle.

These are credential-use permissions. A login can provide the full website
account access available to that login; an API key can provide the permissions
the service gives that key. The implementation does not impose a new read-only
role inside either service. Preventing onward grants is an application rule;
it is not a guarantee that an authorized recipient cannot copy account data or
that a third-party browser provider cannot access an entered credential.

## Execution

Logins fill the requester's supervised local browser, after exact origin and
supported-field inspection. The selected owner password is supplied by the
trusted backend, without switching the active Hermes home to the owner. Owner
TOTP or a hosted owner-only code form can satisfy verification. The one-use code
is consumed in the original requester's task, and automatic resume retains that
requester's source, home and DM.

API requests use `clanker_api_request`: the backend adds the owned or invited key
to a supported authentication header. Calls accept relative paths on the saved
HTTPS origin, reject authentication/Host/Cookie overrides, reject private or
local DNS addresses, pin the connection to a resolved public IP, and verify TLS
against the original hostname. Redirects do not forward authentication. Request
and response sizes are limited. Key values are registered for redaction and
scrubbed from responses. Synthetic transport tests verify these restrictions;
no real external API operation was performed for this change.

Cards use only the requester's supervised local checkout. An invitation lets
the member request a purchase; each exact purchase still needs the **card
owner's** hosted approval and current CVV. The owner sees merchant, order, total,
checkout text and requester. Approval does not transfer the task to the owner.
The handler rechecks the original browser, task, conversation and checkout,
consumes approval and CVV before fill/submission, and refuses replay. Submitted
is not paid; the merchant receipt must be checked. Unsupported payment frames,
wallets, subscriptions and bank approval retain their existing limits.

## Revocation and cookies

Revocation is committed before cleanup and cancels pending delegated code/card
approvals. Secret-bearing browser use is recorded before handoff, with an atomic
active-grant check. This covers a revoke racing between handle resolution and
the usage record. Work already in flight may finish before interruption; the
implementation cannot undo earlier disclosures or completed external actions.

For local Chromium, revoke interrupts the original requester task, closes their
private browsers and deletes their Chromium cookie profile under the guest
execution lock. Cleanup conservatively removes all of that recipient's private
browser state, including sessions used for other valid grants. It preserves the
owner's browser and native vault. An active grant can be used again in a fresh
guest browser after cleanup. API requests have no reusable browser cookies.

If cleanup fails, the grant remains revoked and the recorded usage keeps future
browser/terminal execution blocked. The web UI shows **cleanup pending** and
offers retry. **People with access** also exposes orphan invitations whose
native credential was removed, so that member's access can still be removed or
cleanup retried.

Consumer Browser Tool exposes task stop but no reviewed cookie/session deletion
operation. Its stop result now reports `profile_retained: null` (unknown),
correcting the previous unsupported claim of cookie deletion. A required purge
stops the task, keeps a blocked tombstone, and returns cleanup pending. Repeated
stop/retry does not clear that block. Operator cleanup needs an actual provider
deletion/reconciliation capability before a verified reset can be recorded;
this implementation does not supply that capability.

## Browser routing and unresolved incident work

New cloud state keys include workspace, authenticated requester and resolved
home, independent of the short session name or a shared conversation profile.
State carries an explicit owner marker. Provider session IDs are recorded with
that owner/context, and a recorded collision is refused and quarantined. Legacy
state is not silently adopted by the new namespace. Unknown dispatch outcomes
retain their retry block.

These controls govern Clanker's assignments and known grants. They do not prove
a fresh remote browser lacks another account's pre-existing cookies. Provider
ownership collisions are detected on acknowledgement, after task dispatch;
that check cannot undo observations the provider made before acknowledging.
Free-form remote task instructions are not an account-authorization boundary.
The reported disclosure therefore still requires tracing and invalidating
affected legacy/provider state, a provider-enforced requester isolation and
pre-read authorization design, and real two-requester/DM-handoff acceptance.
Existing login state alone must never be used as permission.

## Verified locally

The canonical Hermes test runner passed **79 tests across five affected files**:
invitations, vault, payments, consumer Browser Tool and managed cloud browser.
Coverage includes all three credential kinds, owner/recipient/workspace checks,
CSRF and forged identity fields, persistence, onward-sharing denial, revoked
access, cleanup failure, same session names/shared profile names, recorded
provider-session collisions, delegated code and payment resume, origin-bound
API requests, TLS/DNS pinning and redirect rejection. Checklist coverage adds
multi-credential sharing, atomic rejection without partial permission changes,
stable handles for retained credentials, revocation of unchecked items, no
automatic sharing of later credentials, and removal of an inactive member.

The actual sandboxed Chromium probe exercised A → B → A with two disposable
homes: owner login, denial of the owner's raw handle to the guest, invited login
fill, owner-only HTTP approval, one guest dummy checkout with an observed dummy
receipt, payment replay denial, CVV consumption, no copied guest vault entry,
guest cookie-profile removal when the login is unchecked in that member's
selection, and preservation of the owner's browser.
The same guest task/session can start a fresh browser after cleanup, while the
revoked login remains denied and an unrelated active card grant remains listed.
Its receipt is
[`2026-10-06-invitation-local-browser.json`](../../verification/evidence/2026-10-06-invitation-local-browser.json).

The visible UI check uses disposable identities and dummy credentials on
loopback. The owner initially selected login and API key; the guest saw those
two entries and no card. Edit access restored that checklist; unchecking the
login and checking the card made guest reload show only API key and card, with
the per-purchase owner-approval label. Desktop and mobile checklists and the
member-level sharing list were visually checked. Removing the member through
the single member row then made guest reload show no saved or invited access.
Screenshots are saved as
`output/playwright/vault-invite-selection-desktop.png`,
`vault-edit-selection-mobile.png` and `vault-sharing-members-mobile.png`.
Earlier per-credential Invite
screenshots represent the superseded design. The missing favicon is unrelated
to invitation behavior.
No mailbox content, real credential, live Slack message, real card
charge or production configuration change is used as verification evidence.

def credential_binding(meta):
    bound = {k: meta.to_dict().get(k) for k in ('kind', 'origin', 'identifier', 'created_at')}
    if meta.login_method=='sms':bound['login_method']='sms'
    return json.dumps(bound, sort_keys=True)


def invitation_origin(meta):
    parsed = urlsplit(meta.origin or '')
    if parsed.scheme != 'https' or not parsed.hostname or parsed.username or parsed.port not in (None, 443):
        raise AccessError('Invitations require a credential bound to an exact HTTPS origin.', 403)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CredentialAccess:
    meta: object
    home: Path
    owner: str
    handle: str
    grant_id: str | None = None

    def public(self):
        result = self.meta.to_dict() | {'id': self.handle}
        if self.grant_id:
            result.update(access='invited', shared_by=self.owner,
                          owner_approval_required=self.meta.kind == 'payment')
        return result

    def secret(self):
        raise AccessError('Kernel credentials are opaque and cannot be resolved locally.', 403)


class Delegations:
    def __init__(self, service):
        self.service = service
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            db.executescript('''
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS credential_grants (
                  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                  recipient TEXT NOT NULL, handle TEXT NOT NULL, binding TEXT NOT NULL,
                  created REAL NOT NULL, revoked REAL);
                CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS credential_grant_active
                  ON credential_grants(team,owner,recipient,handle) WHERE revoked IS NULL;
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS credential_grant_usage (
                  grant_id TEXT NOT NULL, team TEXT NOT NULL, recipient TEXT NOT NULL,
                  home TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL,
                  PRIMARY KEY(grant_id,team,recipient,home));
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS browser_session_owners (
                  provider TEXT NOT NULL, session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                  team TEXT NOT NULL, requester TEXT NOT NULL, context TEXT NOT NULL,
                  PRIMARY KEY(provider,session_id));
            ''')
            # Older installations recorded only the latest guest home. Preserve
            # that marker while allowing every new task context to be retained.
            primary = [row['name'] for row in sorted(db.execute('PRAGMA table_info(credential_grant_usage)'),
                                                    key=lambda row: row['pk']) if row['pk']]
            if primary != ['grant_id', 'team', 'recipient', 'home']:
                db.executescript('''
                    BEGIN IMMEDIATE;
                    ALTER TABLE credential_grant_usage RENAME TO credential_grant_usage_legacy;
                    CREATE TABLE credential_grant_usage (
                      grant_id TEXT NOT NULL, team TEXT NOT NULL, recipient TEXT NOT NULL,
                      home TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL,
                      PRIMARY KEY(grant_id,team,recipient,home));
                    INSERT INTO credential_grant_usage SELECT * FROM credential_grant_usage_legacy;
                    DROP TABLE credential_grant_usage_legacy;
                    COMMIT;
                ''')

    @property
    def store(self):
        return self.service.store

    def own_meta(self, team, owner, handle):
        home = self.service.private_home(team, owner)
        if not isinstance(handle, str):
            raise AccessError('Choose one of your saved credentials.', 403)
        meta = self.service.credential_store(team, owner).get_meta(handle)
        if meta is None or meta.kind not in ('login', 'api_key', 'payment'):
            raise AccessError('This credential does not belong to your vault.', 403)
        return home, meta

    def lookup(self, team, requester, handle):
        home = self.service.private_home(team, requester)
        if not isinstance(handle, str) or len(handle) > 100:
            raise AccessError('Choose a saved or invited credential.', 403)
        meta = self.service.credential_store(team, requester).get_meta(handle)
        if meta is not None:
            return CredentialAccess(meta, home, requester, handle)
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM credential_grants WHERE id=? AND team=? AND recipient=? AND revoked IS NULL',
                             (handle, team, requester)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            raise AccessError('This credential is not available to your Slack account.', 403)
        owner_home = self.service.private_home(team, row['owner'])
        meta = self.service.credential_store(team, row['owner']).get_meta(row['handle'])
        if meta is None or credential_binding(meta) != row['binding']:
            raise AccessError('The invited credential was removed or changed. Ask its owner for a new invitation.', 403)
        return CredentialAccess(meta, owner_home, row['owner'], row['id'], row['id'])

    def resolve(self, turn, handle):
        self.service.assert_private(turn)
        return self.lookup(turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id, handle)

    def items(self, team, requester):
        home = self.service.private_home(team, requester)
        items = [meta.to_dict() for meta in self.service.credential_store(team, requester).list_items()]
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            handles = [row[0] for row in db.execute(
                'SELECT id FROM credential_grants WHERE team=? AND recipient=? AND revoked IS NULL ORDER BY created DESC',
                (team, requester))]
        for handle in handles:
            try:
                items.append(self.lookup(team, requester, handle).public())
            except AccessError:
                continue
        return items

    def invite(self, identity, handle, recipient):
        team, owner = identity['team'], identity['owner']
        home, meta = self.own_meta(team, owner, handle)
        if not isinstance(recipient, str) or recipient == owner:
            raise AccessError('Choose another current Slack member.')
        self.service.validate_member(team, recipient)
        invitation_origin(meta)
        self._shareable(team, owner, home, handle)
        with self.service.lock_for(home), self.store.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            # Recheck while holding the same owner lock as disconnect and fills.
            _, current = self.own_meta(team, owner, handle)
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM credential_grants WHERE team=? AND owner=? AND recipient=? AND handle=? AND revoked IS NULL',
                             (team, owner, recipient, handle)).fetchone()
            if row and row['binding'] == credential_binding(current):
                return dict(row)
            if row:
                raise AccessError('Revoke the previous invitation before inviting this changed credential.', 409)
            grant_id = 'grant_' + secrets.token_hex(16)
            db.execute('INSERT INTO credential_grants VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,NULL)',
                       (grant_id, team, owner, recipient, handle, credential_binding(current), self.store.clock()))
            return dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM credential_grants WHERE id=?', (grant_id,)).fetchone())

    def set_access(self, identity, recipient, handles):
        """Save one member's complete selection atomically; future items stay private."""
        team, owner = identity['team'], identity['owner']
        home = self.service.private_home(team, owner)
        if not isinstance(recipient, str) or recipient == owner:
            raise AccessError('Choose another Slack member.')
        if (not isinstance(handles, list) or len(handles) > 100 or
                any(not isinstance(handle, str) or len(handle) > 100 for handle in handles) or
                len(set(handles)) != len(handles)):
            raise AccessError('Select the credentials to share.')
        if handles:
            self.service.validate_member(team, recipient)
        with self.service.lock_for(home), self.store.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            # Validate the entire selection before writing any permission.
            selected = {}
            for handle in handles:
                _, meta = self.own_meta(team, owner, handle)
                invitation_origin(meta)
                self._shareable(team, owner, home, handle)
                selected[handle] = credential_binding(meta)
            previous = [dict(row) for row in db.execute(
                'SELECT * FROM credential_grants WHERE team=? AND owner=? AND recipient=?',
                (team, owner, recipient))]
            if not handles and not previous:
                raise AccessError('This member has no access to your vault.', 403)
            retained, revoked = {}, []
            for row in previous:
                if row['revoked'] is None:
                    if selected.get(row['handle']) == row['binding']:
                        retained[row['handle']] = row
                    else:
                        db.execute('UPDATE credential_grants SET revoked=? WHERE id=?', (self.store.clock(), row['id']))
                        db.execute("UPDATE requests SET status='cancelled',code_payload=NULL,payment_payload=NULL WHERE grant_id=? AND status IN ('waiting','saved','resumed')", (row['id'],))
                        revoked.append(row['id'])
                elif db.execute('SELECT 1 FROM credential_grant_usage WHERE grant_id=?', (row['id'],)).fetchone():
                    revoked.append(row['id'])
            result, added = [], []
            for handle in handles:
                if handle in retained:
                    row = retained[handle]
                else:
                    grant_id = 'grant_' + secrets.token_hex(16)
                    db.execute('INSERT INTO credential_grants VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,NULL)',
                        (grant_id, team, owner, recipient, handle, selected[handle], self.store.clock()))
                    row = dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM credential_grants WHERE id=?', (grant_id,)).fetchone())
                    added.append(grant_id)
                result.append(row)
            return {'grants': result, 'revoked': revoked, 'added': added}

    def _shareable(self, team, owner, home, handle):
        managed = getattr(self.service, 'kernel_auth', None)
        account = managed.account(team, owner, handle) if managed else None
        if account and account['credential_name']:
            return  # recipients receive a separate task profile, never this owner's cookies
        kernel = getattr(self.service, 'kernel_vault', None)
        if kernel is None or not kernel.metadata.credential_vault(team, owner, home, handle):
            raise AccessError('This credential needs its own isolated Kernel vault before it can be shared. Its owner vault cannot be attached to another member\'s browser.', 409)

    def invitations(self, identity, handle=None):
        home = self.service.private_home(identity['team'],identity['owner'])
        if handle is not None:
            self.own_meta(identity['team'], identity['owner'], handle)
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            rows = [dict(row) for row in db.execute('''
                SELECT g.*, EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM credential_grant_usage u WHERE u.grant_id=g.id) AS used
                FROM credential_grants g WHERE team=? AND owner=? AND (? IS NULL OR handle=?)
                AND (revoked IS NULL OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM credential_grant_usage u WHERE u.grant_id=g.id)) ORDER BY created''',
                (identity['team'], identity['owner'], handle, handle))]
        result = []
        for row in rows:
            meta=self.service.credential_store(identity['team'],identity['owner']).get_meta(row['handle'])
            result.append({k:row[k] for k in ('id','recipient','created','revoked')} | {
                'handle':row['handle'],
                'credential':meta.label if meta else 'Removed credential · '+json.loads(row['binding'])['origin'],
                'cleanup_pending':row['revoked'] is not None and bool(row['used'])})
        return result

    def revoke(self, identity, grant_id):
        self.service.validate_member(identity['team'], identity['owner'])
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM credential_grants WHERE id=? AND team=? AND owner=?',
                             (grant_id, identity['team'], identity['owner'])).fetchone()
            if not row:
                raise AccessError('This invitation does not belong to your vault.', 403)
            db.execute('UPDATE credential_grants SET revoked=COALESCE(revoked,?) WHERE id=?',
                       (self.store.clock(), grant_id))
            db.execute("UPDATE requests SET status='cancelled',code_payload=NULL,payment_payload=NULL WHERE grant_id=? AND status IN ('waiting','saved','resumed')",
                       (grant_id,))
            return dict(row)

    def record_browser_use(self, turn, access):
        if not access.grant_id:
            return
        # Record before any secret-bearing browser I/O, including uncertain I/O.
        self.resolve(turn, access.handle)
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            active = db.execute('SELECT binding FROM credential_grants WHERE id=? AND team=? AND recipient=? AND revoked IS NULL',
                                (access.grant_id, turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id)).fetchone()
            if not active or active['binding'] != credential_binding(access.meta):
                raise AccessError('The invitation was revoked or changed before browser access.', 403)
            db.execute('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO credential_grant_usage VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)',
                       (access.grant_id, turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id,
                'fills, submissions or other mutations; old page references are invalid.', 409)
        data = native._parse_json_result(result.get('result')) if result.get('success') else None
        if isinstance(data, str):
            data = native._parse_json_result(data)
        if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get('values'), list) or not isinstance(data.get('visible'), list):
            raise AccessError('Private browser fields could not be protected for observation.', 409)
        split_values = data.get('split_values', [])
        if not isinstance(split_values, list) or any(not isinstance(value, str) for value in split_values):
            raise AccessError('Private browser fields could not be protected for observation.', 409)
        key = (turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id, str(turn.home.resolve()))
        self._split_redactions[key] = tuple(value for value in split_values if value)
        self.remember_values(turn, data['values'])
        consent = self.service.personal.store(turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id).model_access()
        return any(item is True for item in data['visible']) or bool(data['visible']) and not consent

    def protect_observation(self, turn, tool_name):
        if self.refresh_privacy(turn) and tool_name in {'browser_vision', 'browser_get_images'}:
            raise AccessError('Private fields are still visible. Use the redacted text snapshot until the website finishes verification.', 409)

    def scope(self, team, owner):
        return team, owner, self.service.private_home(team, owner)

    def ensure_vault(self, team, owner):
        scope = self.scope(team, owner)
        # Existing invitations can be resolved while another owner's task lock
        # is held. Reading immutable mappings avoids opposite lock ordering for
        # two members who have invited each other.
        mapping = self.metadata.vault(*scope)
        if mapping:
            return {'id': mapping['vault_id']}
        with self.service.lock_for(scope[2]):
            mapping = self.metadata.vault(*scope)
            if mapping:
                return {'id': mapping['vault_id']}
            name = 'clanker-' + hashlib.sha256(':'.join(map(str, scope)).encode()).hexdigest()[:40]
            # A name is deterministic. An unknown create is reconciled by GET
            # on the next invocation, never by blindly repeating the POST.
            remote = self.client.get_vault(name)
            if remote is None:
                remote = self.client.create_vault(name)
            self.metadata.bind_vault(*scope, remote['id'], name)
            return {'id': remote['id']}

    def browser_vault(self, turn):
        self.service.validate_member(turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id)
        return self.ensure_vault(turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id)

    def browser_vaults(self, turn):
        """Attach this account and only independently authorized dedicated items."""
        team, requester = turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id
        self.service.validate_member(team, requester)
        ids = {self.ensure_vault(team, requester)['id']}
        scope = self.scope(team, requester)
        for binding in self.metadata.list_credential_vaults(*scope):
            record = self.metadata.item(*scope, binding['handle'])
            if record and record['status'] in {'ready', 'pending'}:
                if record['vault_id'] != binding['vault_id'] or record['kind'] == 'personal':
                    raise AccessError('A dedicated credential vault binding is invalid.', 403)
                ids.add(binding['vault_id'])
        with self.metadata.requests.connection() as db:
            grants = [dict(row) for row in db.execute('SELECT id,owner,handle FROM credential_grants '
                'WHERE team=? AND recipient=? AND revoked IS NULL ORDER BY id', (team, requester))]
        for grant in grants:
            access = self.service.delegations.lookup(team, requester, grant['id'])
            if access.owner != grant['owner'] or access.meta.id != grant['handle'] or access.grant_id != grant['id']:
                raise AccessError('An invited credential binding changed.', 403)
            scope = self.scope(team, access.owner)
            record = self.metadata.item(*scope, access.meta.id)
            binding = self.metadata.credential_vault(*scope, access.meta.id)
            if (not record or record['status'] != 'ready' or record['kind'] not in {'login', 'api_key'} or
                    not binding or binding['vault_id'] != record['vault_id']):
                raise AccessError('This invited credential requires a dedicated Kernel vault before browser use.', 403)
            ids.add(binding['vault_id'])
        return [{'id': value} for value in sorted(ids)]

    def native_store(self, team, owner):
        return KernelAccountStore(self, team, owner)

    def record(self, team, owner, handle):
        scope = self.scope(team, owner)
        self.ensure_vault(team, owner)

            raise AccessError('This Kernel credential is unavailable to this Slack account.', 403)
        return record

        """Read an explicitly backend-readable API key for trusted HTTP use only.

        This is not a tool or a general credential resolver. The authenticated
        handle selects an exact owner and immutable Kernel item; ordinary item

        self.service.delegations.check_execution(turn)

            current = self.service.delegations.resolve(turn, handle)

                raise AccessError('This API credential is not ready for backend use.', 403)
            remote = self.client.get_credential(record['vault_id'], record['key'],

# Use ready saved Vault logins before starting empty hosted sign-in

## Finding

Nike had a ready opaque saved phone login, but the Managed Auth dispatcher started a separate empty sign-in path. The existence of a saved handle therefore did not cause its phone field to be filled.

Evidence: [original Slack task](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/D0C6F49F2KD/p1791654214720759); QA run `r20261010-231334-add-one-pair-640d`; Hermes session `20261010_231341_68c95df4`. The original benchmark ran late 10 October through early 11 October 2026 IST. Time-only Kernel correlations are intentionally excluded pending exact-thread recollection.

## Change

For an owned ready Kernel Vault login with no Managed Auth credential or active selection, return the secure-fill route. Kernel fills only declared fields into observed exact-origin controls. Bind the browser to the access handle before secret-bearing I/O, including uncertain fills, and reuse its owned retained profile across threads. The existing private code workflow handles verification without exposing values. Hosted Managed Auth remains preferred when its credential or selection exists.

## Validation and limits

The latest saved-login/profile/Vault/ACL batch passed 66 tests, and the broader auth batch passed 292. Cross-owner and cross-origin access remain denied. Website field acceptance, real Nike sign-in and SMS completion remain live acceptance work. A filled form is not proof of login.

"""Persistent browser identities, separate from task and CDP ownership.

Only opaque provider references and existing credential metadata live here.
Profile writers are durably reserved before dispatch and never expire by time.
Unknown provider outcomes must be reconciled, not retried with another writer.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import secrets

from vault.delegation import credential_binding
from vault.store import AccessError


_PRINCIPAL_FIELDS = ('key', 'profile_name', 'kind', 'team', 'owner',
                     'account_handle', 'origin', 'binding', 'generation')
_LEASE_IDENTITY = ('id', 'principal_key', 'writer_key', 'kind', 'team',
                   'requester', 'home', 'thread')


class ProfileBusy(AccessError):
    def __init__(self, lease):
        super().__init__('This browser profile is in use by another task or sign-in. '
                         'Wait for that work to finish; do not sign in again or create another profile.', 409)
        self.lease = dict(lease)


class ProfileRegistry:
    def __init__(self, service):
        self.service = service
        self.store = service.store
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            db.executescript('''
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS browser_profile_principals (
                    key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, profile_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                    kind TEXT NOT NULL, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                    account_handle TEXT NOT NULL, origin TEXT NOT NULL, binding TEXT NOT NULL,
                    generation INTEGER NOT NULL, profile_id TEXT, state TEXT NOT NULL,
                    created REAL NOT NULL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS browser_profile_selections (
                    team TEXT NOT NULL, requester TEXT NOT NULL, home TEXT NOT NULL,
                    thread TEXT NOT NULL, principal_key TEXT NOT NULL, access_handle TEXT,
                    PRIMARY KEY(team,requester,home,thread));
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS browser_profile_accounts (
                    principal_key TEXT NOT NULL, origin TEXT NOT NULL,
                    owner TEXT NOT NULL, account_handle TEXT NOT NULL, binding TEXT NOT NULL,
                    PRIMARY KEY(principal_key,origin));
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS browser_profile_leases (
                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, principal_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                    writer_key TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, team TEXT NOT NULL,
                    requester TEXT NOT NULL, home TEXT NOT NULL, thread TEXT NOT NULL,
                    remote_id TEXT, state TEXT NOT NULL, created REAL NOT NULL);
            ''')

    def _context(self, turn):
        self.service.assert_private(turn)
        self.service.delegations.check_execution(turn)
        return (turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id, str(turn.home.resolve()),
                turn.source.chat_id + ':' + str(turn.source.thread_id or ''))

    def _access(self, turn, access):
        if access is None:
            return None
        current = self.service.delegations.resolve(turn, access.handle)
        if (current.owner != access.owner or current.meta.id != access.meta.id or
                current.grant_id != access.grant_id or
                credential_binding(current.meta) != credential_binding(access.meta) or
                current.meta.kind != 'login'):
            raise AccessError('The saved browser account or invitation changed.', 403)
        return current

    @staticmethod
    def _key(kind, team, owner, handle=''):
        return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(['browser-principal-v1', kind, team, owner, handle],
                                        separators=(',', ':')).encode()).hexdigest()

    @staticmethod
    def _principal(row):
        return {field: row[field] for field in _PRINCIPAL_FIELDS}

    def get(self, key):
        """Internal metadata read; callers still need authorize before use."""
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM browser_profile_principals WHERE key=?', (key,)).fetchone()
        return self._principal(row) if row else None

    def _verified_principal(self, principal):
        if not isinstance(principal, dict) or not isinstance(principal.get('key'), str):
            raise AccessError('The saved browser profile has no verified identity.', 403)
        current = self.get(principal['key'])
        if current is None or any(principal.get(field) != current[field] for field in _PRINCIPAL_FIELDS):
            raise AccessError('The saved browser profile identity changed.', 403)
        return current

    def resolve(self, turn, access=None):
        context = self._context(turn)

def test_three_people_and_one_shared_login_have_four_profiles(principal_env):
    env = principal_env
    personal = [env.registry.resolve(turn) for turn in env.turns.values()]
    guest = env.grant('UB')
    shared = env.registry.resolve(env.turns['UB'], guest)
    owner = env.service.delegations.resolve(env.turns['UA'], 'groceries')
    assert env.registry.resolve(env.turns['UA'], owner) == shared
    assert len({p['profile_name'] for p in personal + [shared]}) == 4
    for user, turn in env.turns.items():
        another = replace(turn, task_id='next-task', source=replace(turn.source, thread_id='200.2'))
        assert env.registry.resolve(another) == personal[list(env.turns).index(user)]


def test_shared_selection_is_exact_and_does_not_replace_personal_default(principal_env):
    env = principal_env
    access = env.grant('UB')
    turn = env.turns['UB']
    personal = env.registry.selected(turn)
    shared = env.registry.select(turn, access)
    assert shared['kind'] == 'shared' and shared != personal
    assert env.registry.selected(turn) == shared
    assert env.registry.selection_handle(turn) == access.handle
    another = replace(turn, source=replace(turn.source, thread_id='200.2'))
    assert env.registry.selected(another) == personal
    env.registry.release_selection(turn)
    assert env.registry.selected(turn) == personal


def test_different_owned_sites_use_one_personal_profile(principal_env):
    env = principal_env
    turn = env.turns['UA']
    profiles = [env.registry.select(turn, env.service.delegations.resolve(turn, handle))
                for handle in ('docs', 'code')]
    assert profiles[0]['profile_name'] == profiles[1]['profile_name']
    assert profiles[0]['kind'] == 'personal'


def test_shared_profile_survives_last_grant_revocation_for_owner(principal_env):
    env = principal_env
    access = env.grant('UB')
    shared = env.registry.select(env.turns['UB'], access)
    env.service.delegations.revoke({'team': 'TT', 'owner': 'UA'}, access.grant_id)
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):
        env.registry.selected(env.turns['UB'])
    owned = env.service.delegations.resolve(env.turns['UA'], 'groceries')
    assert env.registry.resolve(env.turns['UA'], owned) == shared


def test_browser_and_login_writers_are_exclusive_across_threads(principal_env):
    from cloud_browser.profile_registry import ProfileBusy
    env = principal_env
    turn = env.turns['UA']
    principal = env.registry.selected(turn)
    lease = env.registry.acquire(turn, principal, 'browser-one')
    other = replace(turn, source=replace(turn.source, thread_id='200.2'))
    with pytest.raises(ProfileBusy) as caught:
        env.registry.acquire(other, principal, 'auth-two', kind='auth')
    assert caught.value.lease['id'] == lease['id']
    env.registry.release(lease)
    assert env.registry.acquire(other, principal, 'auth-two', kind='auth')['kind'] == 'auth'


def test_uncertain_writer_never_expires_or_replays(principal_env):

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_owned_identity_survives_isolated_tasks_and_multiple_domains(persistent):
    f = persistent
    a = f.task()
    first, old = await complete(f, a)
    f.auth.release_context('TT', 'UA', a.home, thread=f.service.cloud_browser.thread(a))
    assert old['profile_name'] in f.remote.profiles
    before = deepcopy(mutations(f))
    b = f.task(thread='201.1')
    result = await f.auth.authenticate(b, handle=first['handle'])
    assert result['status'] == 'authenticated' and result['session_reused']
    assert mutations(f) == before
    assert f.auth.browser_binding(b)['profile_name'] == old['profile_name']
    other, second = await complete(f, f.task(thread='202.1'), 'https://second.example')
    assert second['profile_name'] == old['profile_name']
    assert second['connection_id'] != old['connection_id']
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):
        await f.auth.authenticate(f.task('UB'), handle=first['handle'])
    _, foreign = await complete(f, f.task('UB'), ORIGIN)
    assert foreign['profile_name'] != old['profile_name']
    f.auth.cleanup_home(a.home)
    assert old['profile_name'] in f.remote.profiles
    assert second['connection_id'] in f.remote.connections
    assert f.auth.browser_binding(b) is None

async def test_owned_identity_survives_isolated_tasks_and_multiple_domains(persistent):
    f = persistent
    a = f.task()
    first, old = await complete(f, a)

Current sharing is **account-based in the UI**, but account discovery remains coarse.

1. **Supported flow:** Open Vault → **Manage access** → choose an onboarded Slack member → check accounts → consent → **Invite**. The recipient immediately receives access and a Slack DM, then sees **Shared with you**. Edit/remove from **People with access**. Source: [page.html](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/page.html:38), [service.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:181).

2. **Permissions:** Each grant binds workspace, owner, recipient, credential handle, and immutable credential metadata; it does not copy the secret into the recipient’s vault. Only owned accounts can be shared, members must be authorized/current, onward sharing is refused, and changed/deleted account metadata invalidates grants. Exact handle resolution is a primary-key query. Source: [delegation.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/delegation.py:52), [delegation.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/delegation.py:97).

3. **Current profiles are already deterministic:** Once the account handle is selected, `ProfileRegistry` derives the profile from `(workspace, owner, account_handle)` for shared accounts. All invitees plus the owner use that account’s shared profile; different unshared owned sites use one personal profile. The code does **not** search all browser profiles for the right cookies. Source: [profile_registry.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/profile_registry.py:96). Tests explicitly cover “three people and one shared login have four profiles” and owner/recipient profile equality: [test_browser_profile_principals.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/probes/test_browser_profile_principals.py:46).

4. **The user's scale concern exists one layer earlier:** `clanker_vault_list` lists all requester-owned and invited items. If authentication receives only an origin, it materializes all accessible metadata and filters in Python. Multiple accounts at the same origin return `account_choice_required`; no project/team/purpose/default binding resolves the ambiguity. `Delegations.items()` also performs lookup per grant, and `ManagedAuth.account()` loads all owner accounts then uses `next(...)`. Sources: [managed_auth.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:710), [delegation.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/delegation.py:119), [managed_auth.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:123).

5. **Other 100-person limitations:** Sharing accepts one recipient per operation, with at most 100 selected handles for that recipient; there is no group or bulk-recipient ACL. The member chooser loads every ready member and sequentially calls Slack `users_info`, and the invitation checklist renders all owned accounts. One shared profile also permits only **one browser/auth writer at a time**, so many users of the *same account* contend even when resolution is perfect. Sources: [delegation.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/delegation.py:156), [service.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:148), [profile_registry.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/profile_registry.py:49).

Architectural framing to use: **resolve intended authorized account first; profile is an internal execution resource derived afterward.** Improve account lookup and context selection, rather than expose a profile picker or ask the model to inspect hundreds of profiles. Distinguish 100 different services (origin can narrow directly) from 100 accounts at one service (requires meaningful account identity/context; indexing cannot infer intent).

Old October 6 decision documentation describes superseded native/local vault and per-recipient profile behavior. Prefer current source above. No live invitation or 100-account performance test was performed.
